editorialIntro.eyebrow: A GUIDE TO SHIPS, ITINERARIES & PORTS
editorialIntro.heading: The Last Frontier Meets the Finest Cuisine at Sea
paragraphs: Oceania Alaska cruises combine the dramatic scenery of America's Last Frontier with the line's smaller-ship atmosphere, destination-focused itineraries and culinary experiences. Guests can explore glacier-carved waterways, historic Gold Rush communities, coastal fishing towns and wildlife-rich landscapes before returning to an elegant ship with open-seating restaurants and personalized service.

For the 2027 Alaska season, Oceania Cruises has announced voyages aboard Oceania Riviera, with seven-, 10- and 11-day itineraries departing from Seattle and Vancouver. The program includes well-known ports such as Juneau, Ketchikan and Sitka, as well as less familiar destinations including Wrangell, Klawock and Haines. Selected voyages also feature scenic cruising through Holkham Bay Glacier Fjords or past Hubbard Glacier.

The best Oceania Alaska cruise depends on how much time you have, which ports you want to visit, whether you prefer a round-trip sailing or a one-way journey, and how much time you want to spend exploring Alaska before or after your cruise.
This guide explains the ships, itineraries, ports, shore excursions, onboard experience and practical planning considerations to help you choose the right voyage.

items.title: Oceania Riviera: Featured Alaska Ship
items.description: For the announced 2027 Alaska season, Oceania Riviera is the featured ship. It combines the line's culinary focus with a comfortable onboard environment for exploring Alaska's coastal communities and scenic waterways.
bulletPoints: Carries 1,250 guests in an intimate, uncrowded luxury atmosphere
Offers a wide range of public spaces, comfortable lounges, and accommodation categories
Designed for a relaxed onboard experience between port calls

items.title: Onboard Highlights & Culinary Program
items.description: The ship's culinary program is particularly relevant in Alaska, where regional seafood, local ingredients and destination-inspired menus can complement the experiences ashore.

The Grand Dining Room for a varied menu and classic dining experience
Polo Grill for steakhouse-style dining and Toscana for Italian-inspired cuisine

items.title: Why Ship Choice Matters in Alaska
items.description: In Alaska, the ship is more than a place to sleep between ports. You may spend time watching mountains, forests, islands and glaciers from the deck or your stateroom veranda.
bulletPoints: Veranda access: A private outdoor space can be valuable for enjoying the scenery
Public viewing areas: Look for comfortable places to watch scenic cruising
Dining variety: Consider the restaurants and menus available on the specific ship
Voyage length: A longer sailing may offer more ports and a different pace
Embarkation and disembarkation: Seattle and Vancouver offer different pre- and post-cruise travel opportunities
Do not assume that every Oceania ship operates every Alaska itinerary. Check the ship assigned to the exact sailing

itinerariesOverview.title: Oceania Alaska Cruise Itineraries
itinerariesOverview.subtitle: Oceania's announced 2027 Alaska program includes seven-, 10- and 11-day voyages, offering distinct ways to experience the region.

items.title: 7-Day Alaska Cruises: Visions of Alaska
items.description: A practical choice for travelers with limited vacation time who want a convenient round-trip sailing. Operates roundtrip from Seattle, calling at Ketchikan, Icy Strait Point, Sitka, and Victoria (British Columbia). Ideal for first-time Alaska cruisers and those combining a cruise with a Pacific Northwest land stay.
items.subtitle: Roundtrip from Seattle

items.title: 10-Day Alaska Cruises: Deeper Coastal Immersion
items.description: Provides more time in Alaska with additional ports and diverse scenic cruising. Features both roundtrip Seattle sailings and one-way journeys between Vancouver and Seattle, visiting Ketchikan, Sitka, Wrangell, Icy Strait Point, and Haines for travelers seeking smaller coastal towns.
items.subtitle: Seattle Roundtrip & Vancouver Connectors

items.title: 11-Day Alaska Cruises: Comprehensive Wilderness
items.description: A slower, comprehensive coastal journey between Vancouver and Seattle (or reverse). Calls include Juneau, Ketchikan, Sitka, Haines, Wrangell, and Klawock, offering more scenic cruising through Holkham Bay or past Hubbard Glacier with fewer sea days.
items.subtitle: One-Way Vancouver & Seattle Journeys

items.title: 27-Day Transpacific Collector: Alaska to Japan
items.description: An extraordinary extended journey departing Vancouver, cruising the Alaska Inside Passage, visiting Hubbard Glacier and Dutch Harbor in the Aleutians, and crossing the Pacific Ocean to Tokyo, Japan. Perfect for travelers seeking a world-class grand voyage.
items.subtitle: Grand Transoceanic Voyage

popularPorts.title: Best Alaska Ports to Visit on an Oceania Cruise
popularPorts.subtitle: From historic Gold Rush towns and Indigenous cultural centers to wildlife sanctuaries and glacier gateways.

items.title: Juneau: Mendenhall Glacier & Whale Watching
items.description: Accessible only by sea or air, Alaska's capital offers helicopter glacier flightseeing, dog sledding on icefields, scenic whale-watching excursions in Auke Bay, and the Mount Roberts Tramway.

items.title: Ketchikan: Totem Poles & Historic Creek Street
items.description: Set on the edge of the Tongass National Forest, Ketchikan is famous for historic over-water boardwalks at Creek Street, rich Tlingit and Haida totem pole art, and floating oyster farm culinary tours.

items.title: Sitka: Coastal Fjords & Baranof Island
items.description: Former capital of Russian America, Sitka features St. Michael's Russian Orthodox Cathedral, the Sitka National Historical Park totem trail, sea otter boat quests, and coastal rainforest trails.

items.title: Skagway: Gold Rush Streets & White Pass Railway
items.description: Step into 1898 along preserved wooden boardwalks and false-front saloons. Board the vintage White Pass & Yukon Route narrow-gauge railroad climbing 3,000 feet past roaring waterfalls and mountain passes.

items.title: Icy Strait Point: Hoonah & Marine Wildlife
items.description: Owned and operated by local Huna Tlingit Native people, offering world-class brown bear viewing in Spasski River valley, humpback whale tours, and coastal kayaking.

items.title: Haines, Wrangell & Klawock: Authentic Small-Town Alaska
items.description: Less-visited ports accessed by smaller ships: Haines (Chilkat bald eagles and dramatic peaks), Wrangell (Petroglyph Beach and Anan Bear Observatory), and Klawock (authentic Prince of Wales totem carving).

glacierScenery.title: Glacier Scenery on an Oceania Alaska Cruise

regent.title: Steep Granite Walls & Tidewater Ice
regent.description: Holkham Bay is celebrated for dramatic fjord scenery, sheer granite cliff walls soaring thousands of feet, and pristine ice-carved waterways. As Oceania Riviera navigates these narrow channels, guests observe floating azure icebergs, roaring waterfalls, harbor seals resting on ice floes, and towering glaciers from panoramic viewing decks.
features: Scenic cruising through dramatic fjord landscapes
Viewing from the comfort of the ship's open decks and private verandas
Harbor seals pupping on floating ice bergs and cascading waterfalls
Intimate waterways inaccessible to mega-resort cruise ships

viking.title: North America's Largest Tidewater Giant
viking.description: Hubbard Glacier is one of Alaska's most magnificent natural wonders. Spanning more than six miles across its face and towering up to 400 feet above the water, this active advancing glacier frequently calves massive ice chunks into Disenchantment Bay with a thunderous roar known as "white thunder."
features: Enormous six-mile-wide ice face rising 400 feet above water
Active calving with thunderous echoing splashes into the bay
Narrated by onboard naturalists and destination specialists
Surrounded by snow-capped peaks of the Saint Elias Mountains

shoreExcursions.title: Oceania Alaska Shore Excursions
shoreExcursions.subtitle: Immerse yourself in wildlife, glaciers, culinary traditions, and native heritage across Alaska's coastal wilderness.

items.title: Wildlife & Whale-Watching Encounters
items.description: Board custom high-speed catamarans in Auke Bay or Icy Strait Point with expert naturalists to observe humpback whales breaching, orcas hunting, sea otters rafting, and bald eagles nesting in old-growth trees.

items.title: Helicopter Flightseeing & Glacier Trekking
items.description: Soar over the dramatic jagged crevasses of the Juneau Icefield or Taku Glacier before touching down for a guided walk atop ancient glacial ice with crampons and specialized ice gear.

items.title: Dog Sledding on Glaciers & Kennels
items.description: Meet Alaskan husky sled dogs and Iditarod mushers. Fly via helicopter to high-altitude glacier camps for an authentic dogsled ride across pristine snowpack, or tour historic working training kennels.

items.title: Chef-Led Culinary & Seafood Tours
items.description: Oceania's exclusive culinary excursions: visit Ketchikan's floating oyster farms, sample wild Dungeness crab and Pacific salmon, and participate in master cooking classes back onboard in the Culinary Center.

items.title: Tlingit Heritage & Gold Rush History
items.description: Explore authentic Native clan houses, watch master totem carvers at work in Klawock, or ride the vintage White Pass & Yukon Route narrow-gauge railway tracing the footsteps of 1898 gold prospectors.

whichItineraryToChoose.title: Which Oceania Alaska Itinerary Should You Choose?
whichItineraryToChoose.subtitle: Matching your available vacation time, departure preferences, and travel style to the ideal route

bestFor.title: First-Time Alaska Cruisers
bestFor.description: A convenient 7-day sailing covering marquee ports (Ketchikan, Sitka, Icy Strait Point) with simple round-trip domestic flights.

bestFor.title: Straightforward Travel Logistics
bestFor.description: Embark and disembark in the same U.S. city (Seattle), eliminating international airport transfers and one-way airfare surcharges.

bestFor.title: Combining Seattle Sightseeing
bestFor.description: Easily add a 2-night pre- or post-cruise stay to explore Pike Place Market, the Space Needle, and Chihuly Garden and Glass.

bestFor.title: Includes Victoria, British Columbia
bestFor.description: Features a charming Canadian evening call at Victoria's picturesque Inner Harbour.

notFor.title: More Days & Deeper Exploration
notFor.description: 10 and 11 days allow you to visit smaller, authentic ports like Wrangell, Haines, and Klawock with fewer sea days.

notFor.title: Scenic Glacier Cruising
notFor.description: Expanded routing provides scenic cruising through Holkham Bay Glacier Fjords or past the advancing face of Hubbard Glacier.

notFor.title: Two World-Class Departure Cities
notFor.description: Experience both cosmopolitan Vancouver (Stanley Park, Gastown) and energetic Seattle in a single vacation.

notFor.title: Ideal for Land Extension Tours
notFor.description: Seamlessly connect with Rocky Mountaineer train tours into the Canadian Rockies or flights up into Denali National Park.

bestTimeToSail.title: Best Time to Take an Oceania Alaska Cruise
bestTimeToSail.description: Alaska's main cruise season generally runs from spring through early autumn. The experience changes throughout the season, so your preferred travel month matters.

items.title: May
items.description: May can offer a quieter start to the Alaska cruise season. Travelers may encounter cooler temperatures and early-season conditions. Consider May if you prefer: Earlier-season travel, potentially fewer crowds than peak summer, and a focus on scenery and coastal communities. Weather and excursion availability can vary.

items.title: June
items.description: June brings longer daylight hours and the beginning of the summer travel period. It may appeal to travelers who want: Extended daylight for sightseeing, opportunities for wildlife and outdoor activities, and a summer atmosphere in Alaska's ports.

items.title: July
items.description: July is a popular month for Alaska cruises. It generally offers a full summer travel experience, although visitor numbers can be higher. Consider booking early if you have specific cabin, itinerary or excursion preferences.

items.title: August
items.description: August can be a good option for travelers who want summer conditions and a different seasonal atmosphere from early summer. Weather remains variable, and rain is possible.

items.title: September
items.description: September offers a later-season experience, with changing landscapes and a transition toward autumn. Travelers should pay attention to the exact sailing date, excursion schedules and weather-related considerations.

whatToPack.title: What to Pack for an Oceania Alaska Cruise
whatToPack.subtitle: A versatile layered packing strategy is essential for Alaska's rapidly changing coastal microclimates.

categories.title: The Essential Layering System
categories.description: Plan for three functional layers rather than one heavy winter coat: moisture-wicking base, insulating fleece mid-layer, and waterproof outer shell.
items: High-performance waterproof, breathable hooded rain shell
Warm fleece jacket, wool sweater, or lightweight down jacket
Moisture-wicking thermal base layer tops and bottoms
Quick-drying hiking trousers and comfortable casual pants

categories.title: Outdoor Gear & Glacier Viewing
categories.description: Deck viewing in glacier fjords can be breezy and chilly. Proper accessories ensure hours of comfortable wildlife spotting.
items: Waterproof walking shoes or sturdy trail sneakers with deep traction
Warm fleece beanie hat and touchscreen-compatible gloves
Polarized sunglasses and UV sunscreen (glacier ice reflection is intense)

categories.title: Onboard Elegant Casual Evening Attire
categories.description: Oceania follows an elegant casual dress code in the evenings. Formal tuxedos and evening gowns are never required.
items: Collared shirts, sweaters, and tailored slacks for men
Stylish dresses, elegant separates, or pantsuits for women
Smart loafers or dress shoes for evening dining venues
Warm wrap or light jacket for starlit evening deck strolls

Fresh coastal air and unobstructed wildlife photography

items.name: Concierge Level Veranda

Priority specialty dining and shore excursion reservations
Complimentary pressing of garments upon embarkation
Prime mid-ship and higher-deck panoramic locations

items.name: Penthouse Suites with Butler

Oversized private veranda with teak lounge chairs and dining table
Priority tender embarkation and VIP disembarkation privileges

landStayExtensions.title: Adding a Land Stay Before or After Your Alaska Cruise
landStayExtensions.subtitle: Extend your coastal voyage into the dramatic interior of Alaska or the Canadian Rockies.

items.title: Denali National Park & Interior Alaska
items.description: Journey north into the heart of Alaska aboard glass-domed luxury railcars. Spend 3 to 5 nights exploring Denali's six million acres of wilderness, viewing Mount Denali (20,310 ft), grizzly bears, moose, and caribou.

items.title: Vancouver & British Columbia
items.description: Add 2 to 3 nights in Vancouver before or after your one-way cruise. Walk the seawall at Stanley Park, explore historic Gastown, visit Granville Island Market, and take the Capilano Suspension Bridge excursion.

items.title: The Canadian Rockies & Rocky Mountaineer
items.description: Connect your Vancouver sailing with the world-famous Rocky Mountaineer luxury train through the Canadian Rockies, visiting Banff, Lake Louise, and Jasper with five-star Fairmont resort stays.

items.title: Seattle & Pacific Northwest
items.description: Pair your Seattle roundtrip with a weekend exploring Pike Place Market, Washington wine tastings in Woodinville, or a day trip to Mount Rainier National Park before embarking on Oceania Riviera.

items.title: Custom Land-and-Sea Curation
items.description: Trips & Ships Luxury Travel coordinates seamless transfers, five-star luxury hotel reservations, and private guided land excursions to complement your Oceania Alaska cruise.

bookingSteps.title: How to Book the Right Oceania Alaska Cruise
bookingSteps.subtitle: Choosing the right sailing requires more than selecting a departure date. Compare the itinerary, stateroom, fare conditions and travel arrangements together.

steps.title: Choose Your Preferred Travel Dates
steps.description: Start with your available vacation dates and compare the sailings that operate during that period.

steps.title: Decide Between Seattle and Vancouver
steps.description: Consider whether a round-trip or one-way itinerary is more convenient. Include airfare, hotel stays and transfers in the comparison.

steps.title: Compare the Port List
steps.description: Review every port and scenic cruising day. Look for the destinations that matter most to you rather than relying only on the itinerary title.

steps.title: Select Your Stateroom
steps.description: Compare inside, oceanview, veranda and suite categories. Consider the price difference and how you plan to use the stateroom.

steps.title: Review the Fare and Inclusions
steps.description: Check the exact Your World Included benefits, beverage options, shore excursion credit and any promotional terms attached to your booking.

steps.title: Plan Shore Excursions
steps.description: Identify excursions that are important to you, particularly limited-capacity activities such as helicopter tours and selected wildlife experiences.

steps.title: Arrange Flights and Hotels
steps.description: For one-way itineraries, make sure your arrival and departure arrangements match the embarkation and disembarkation ports.

steps.title: Consider a Land Extension
steps.description: If you want to experience Denali, the Canadian Rockies or other inland destinations, allow enough time for a properly planned extension.

faqs.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Oceania Alaska Cruises
faqs.subtitle: Clear, verified answers to the most common questions when planning an Oceania Alaska voyage

questions.question: Does Oceania Cruises sail to Alaska?
questions.answer: Yes. Oceania Cruises offers Alaska itineraries. Its announced 2027 Alaska season features Oceania Riviera, with seven-, 10- and 11-day voyages departing from Seattle and Vancouver.

questions.question: Which Oceania ship sails to Alaska in 2027?
questions.answer: Oceania Riviera is the ship announced for the 2027 Alaska season. Always check the ship assigned to the specific departure when booking.

questions.question: How long are Oceania Alaska cruises?
questions.answer: The announced 2027 program includes seven-, 10- and 11-day cruises. Longer journeys combining Alaska with transpacific destinations to Tokyo are also available.

questions.question: Where do Oceania Alaska cruises depart from?
questions.answer: The announced 2027 Alaska itineraries include departures from Seattle, Washington, and Vancouver, British Columbia.

questions.question: What ports does Oceania visit in Alaska?
questions.answer: Depending on the itinerary, ports can include Juneau, Ketchikan, Sitka, Skagway, Haines, Wrangell, Klawock and Icy Strait Point.

questions.question: Does Oceania visit Hubbard Glacier?
questions.answer: Selected Oceania Alaska itineraries include scenic cruising near Hubbard Glacier. Check the exact voyage details because routes vary.

questions.question: Does Oceania cruise through Holkham Bay Glacier Fjords?
questions.answer: Yes. Holkham Bay Glacier Fjords feature in selected announced 2027 itineraries, providing dramatic fjord scenic cruising from the ship.

questions.question: Is a seven-day Oceania Alaska cruise enough?
questions.answer: A seven-day cruise can be a good introduction to Alaska, particularly for travelers with limited vacation time. It will not visit every port, so compare the itinerary carefully.

questions.question: Is a 10- or 11-day Alaska cruise better?
questions.answer: A longer cruise offers additional ports, more time in the region, and a slower pace. The best option depends on your available vacation time and port preferences.

questions.question: What is the best month for an Oceania Alaska cruise?
questions.answer: May through September are the primary cruise months. June and July offer long daylight hours and warmth, while May and September provide quieter shoulder-season travel.

questions.question: Can I see whales on an Oceania Alaska cruise?
questions.answer: Yes. Whales inhabit Alaska's coastal waters, and ports like Juneau and Icy Strait Point offer world-class whale-watching excursions. Sightings depend on wildlife activity.

questions.question: Are shore excursions included on Oceania Alaska cruises?
questions.answer: Qualifying bookings under Your World Included offer a choice of a shore excursion credit. Excursions beyond an applicable credit carry extra costs.

questions.question: Does Oceania include drinks on Alaska cruises?
questions.answer: Your World Included covers specialty coffees, teas, sodas, and Vero Water. Qualifying bookings can select complimentary wine and beer by the glass during restaurant lunch and dinner hours.

questions.question: Is specialty dining included on Oceania Alaska cruises?
questions.answer: Yes. Dining at all specialty restaurants (Polo Grill, Toscana, Red Ginger) is included in the cruise fare without cover charges.

questions.question: Is Wi-Fi included on Oceania Alaska cruises?
questions.answer: Yes. Complimentary Starlink Wi-Fi is included for all staterooms and suites under the published Your World Included program.
